intro: Convert foot pounds to Nm (pound-feet to newton-meters) accurately for wheel lug nuts, cylinder head bolts, and engine dynamometer curves. Under the International Yard and Pound Agreement, 1 pound-foot (ft·lbf) equals exactly 1.35581795 newton-meters (ft lbs to newton metres), while 1 N·m equals 0.737562 lb·ft. Whether tightening suspension hardware or converting ft/lbs to Nm on service datasheets, multiply by 1.35582 or scan the torque table below.
alsoWrittenAs: ft-lbs to Nm, ft lbs to newton metres, foot pound torque to N·m, ft pounds of torque, lb·ft to N·m

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Torque (ft·lbs → N·m) vs. Force (lbs → N) & ft/lbs Notation
items: Foot-pounds (lb·ft) measure rotational torque, not linear force. Multiply lb·ft by 1.35582 to get N·m; if you instead want to convert pounds-force (lbf) to newtons (N), multiply by 4.44822.

Mechanics often write 'ft/lbs' informally, even though torque multiplies force by distance (ft·lb). Also keep pound-feet separate from pound-inches (1 lb·ft = 12 lb·in) to prevent 12× over-torquing small bolts.

faqs.question: How do you convert ft-lbs to newton-meters (vs. lbs to newtons)?
faqs.answer: For rotational torque, multiply foot-pounds (lb·ft) by 1.35581795 to get newton-meters (N·m)—for example, 100 lb·ft = 135.58 N·m. For linear force (pounds-force, lbf, to newtons, N), multiply lbf by 4.44822 instead.

faqs.question: How many foot-pounds are in a newton-meter?
faqs.answer: There are 0.737562 foot-pounds (lb·ft) in 1 newton-meter (N·m). Conversely, 1 foot-pound equals 1.35581795 newton-meters.

faqs.question: What is 100 ft-lbs in Nm?
faqs.answer: 100 ft-lbs equals 135.58179 N·m (commonly rounded to 136 N·m on metric torque wrenches).
